title: Worker detail operator page with scheduling, placement, assignments, and actions
intended_behavior: The worker detail page presents the worker name, full pubkey, separate liveness and scheduling badges, and state-aware quick actions for cordon, uncordon, drain, undrain, maintenance enter, and maintenance exit.
The scheduling section shows scheduling state, scheduling note or drain reason, queue depth, max concurrency, accepting-new-work status, drain remaining assignment count, and pinned blocker count.

The capabilities and resources sections render generic worker capabilities plus ML capability compatibility fields, host resources, accelerator inventory, and total accelerator memory from the current worker domain shape.
The labels and placement section renders worker labels, example placement selectors, copy-selector actions, and a labels update action that publishes a worker.labels.update.request command.
The active assignments section renders assignment read-model fields when present, distinguishes movable versus pinned or blocked work, and highlights drain blockers.
The pricing section renders advertised worker pricing tiers without depending on stale pseudo-fields.
observed_baseline: Before this slice, web/src/routes/workers/[pubkey]/+page.svelte showed current domain worker capacity, capabilities, resources, accelerators, software, runtime target, pricing, relays, and timestamps.
Before this slice, the detail page did not expose scheduling state, labels, assignment/drain read-model fields, or Nostr worker-management command actions.
out_of_scope: Backend Go code, worker read-model projection implementation, scheduling enforcement, MCP worker tools, workers list page, inference page, and environment pages.
Fixing the concurrent syntax error in web/src/routes/ml/+page.svelte.
